# ux.sgit.ai: UX, measured

> Where the sgit.ai sites, and the browsers and platforms they are read on, fail their readers, measured, and what fixes it. A register of UX failures and gaps across the sgit.ai sites, each measured on the
> live site with a date and version, the principle it breaks, the fix, and (where one exists) a working
> prototype of the fix in three design directions.

Site version: v0.5.0 (2026-10-28). Content CC BY 4.0. Code Apache 2.0. Author: Dinis Cruz, with AI co-authorship.

## The headline

63 findings across 5 products: 55 still open, 16 of them high severity, 8 fixed. 44 are failures (something works against the reader) and 19 are gaps (something the reader needs is not there). Every count on this site is generated from /data/findings.json.

## Properties agents may rely on

- /data/findings.json is the register. Every finding page, list, filter and count is generated from it at build, and the gate fails if a page is stale.
- Every finding has a stable page at /findings/<ID>.html and a markdown twin at /findings/<ID>.md.
- Every page has a markdown twin: replace .html with .md, or append index.md to a directory URL.
- /findings/?product=&area=&problem=&visibility=&recommendation=&principle=&severity=&status=&kind=&q= is a linkable filter (comma-separate values for OR). /browse/ lists every value of every facet with its count.
- /data/taxonomy.json defines the problem, visibility and recommendation vocabularies; /data/site.json defines the products.
- Statuses carry the date and version they were last checked. Nothing here claims to be current beyond that date.
- /llms-full.txt is the whole site in one fetch.

## The pages

/about/  (/about/index.md)
  Who writes ux.sgit.ai, why the register is public, what it is not, and the licences.
/admin/  (/admin/index.md)
  How ux.sgit.ai is built and checked: the source files, the build, the gate, and what CI enforces.
/admin/versions.html  (/admin/versions.md)
  The release history of ux.sgit.ai: each version, its date, what it changed and the files it touched.
/browse/  (/browse/index.md)
  Every index of the register in one place: by product, area, problem, visibility, recommendation, principle, severity, status and kind, each value with its count and a link to the filtered list.
/exemplars/EX-001.html  (/exemplars/EX-001.md)
  It is predictable. The trigger is a small distance scrolled, which the reader controls, not the speed of the gesture, so it behaves the same every time and is learned after one or two uses. The collapsed state is small enough to be a fair trade for the space, and getting there costs only a couple of lines of scroll, so the reader never loses their place to reach it.
/exemplars/EX-002.html  (/exemplars/EX-002.md)
  Seeing your words appear is proof that they are being captured. It is the reason the reporter uses this input over others: as long as the text keeps appearing, they know the recording is safe, and they can keep their attention on what they are saying.
/exemplars/  (/exemplars/index.md)
  Things that work, each kept as the reference for the findings it answers: measured like a finding, with why it works and what it still does not do.
/findings/  (/findings/index.md)
  The register: every UX failure and gap found on the sgit.ai sites, with status, severity, the principle it breaks and the fix. Filterable, and every filter is a link.
/  (/index.md)
  A register of where the sgit.ai sites fail their readers, measured on the live site with a date and a version, the principle each failure breaks, the fix, and a working prototype of it.
/lab/  (/lab/index.md)
  Four encrypted vaults that try the newsroom review's fixes as working prototypes, on the real newsroom data, in three design directions each, before anything changes on the live site.
/method/  (/method/index.md)
  How a UX finding is made here: the reader's path, the stranger test, the review panel, what severity and status mean, and how to file a finding in the register.
/principles/  (/principles/index.md)
  The rules the findings break, each with why it matters, a one-minute test you can run on any page, and the findings that break it.
/reviews/  (/reviews/index.md)
  The full UX reviews the findings come from, published whole, with their date, the version reviewed and the method.
/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.html  (/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md)
  The UX review of newsroom.sgit.ai (v0.6.4, re-checked on v0.7.1) that seeded this site's register: first visit, findability, the article and its feedback, personas, reader primitives, the publishing pipeline and a roadmap.

/about/  ·  /about/index.md
==============================================================================

# Why this exists

The sgit.ai sites are written in the open by Dinis Cruz with teams of AI agents, and they move fast: the newsroom shipped 73 articles in eight weeks. The content is strong. The way a stranger gets into it often is not, because the people who build a site are the last people able to see it as a stranger does.

This site is where that gets written down. Publicly, because a failure stated in the open gets fixed, and because the patterns repeat: an unlabelled number, a filter you cannot share, a rating that starts preselected. Anyone building a site, ours or not, can use the [principles](/principles/index.md) and their one-minute tests.

## Who writes it

Dinis Cruz, with AI co-authorship. Reviews are run by agents playing named roles (architect, librarian, historian, designer, editor, journalist) against measured evidence, and checked by a person. Findings come from those reviews and from anyone who uses the sites and tells us where they got stuck.

## Disclosure

Every site reviewed here is ours. Browsers and platforms appear only where they get in the way of reading our sites, because readers blame the page for them either way, and each such finding names its real owner. The sgit.ai sites argue for sgit (encrypted git for humans and agents) and RiskMandate (behaviour policies for agents), and the author builds both. This site has an interest in those sites working, which is the reason it exists, and no interest in hiding where they do not.

## What this is not

- **Not a style guide.** How code is written is [coding.sgit.ai](https://coding.sgit.ai/). This is what the reader experiences.
- **Not a live monitor.** Every status is dated. Nothing here claims to be current beyond the date it was checked.
- **Not a scorecard of people.** A finding is about a page and a reader, never about who built it.

## Licences

Content CC BY 4.0: take it, adapt it, build on it, with attribution. Code Apache 2.0. The newsroom review quotes and measures newsroom.sgit.ai, which is also CC BY 4.0.


==============================================================================
/admin/  ·  /admin/index.md
==============================================================================

# How it is built

A static site, generated by a small Python build with no dependencies, served as plain files. No framework, no client-side rendering: every page is complete HTML before any script runs, and the one script on the site (the findings filter) only hides and shows rows that are already there.

## The files

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `data/findings.json` | The register. The source of every finding page, list, filter and count |
| `data/exemplars.json` | What good looks like: things that work, each linked to the findings it answers |
| `data/principles.json` | The principles, each with a rule, a reason and a test |
| `data/taxonomy.json` | The problem, visibility and recommendation vocabularies findings are indexed by |
| `data/lab.json` | The design lab: vaults and read keys, directions, screenshots, decisions |
| `data/site.json` | Name, navigation, the products findings belong to (sites, platform, prototypes, browsers), the sibling sites |
| `data/versions.json` | The release history; the first entry is the current version |
| `content/**/*.md` | Hand-written pages, with `{{directives}}` the build fills from the data |
| `admin/build/build.py` | Builds every `.html`, its `.md` twin, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `sitemap.xml` |
| `admin/build/md.py` | The markdown renderer (stdlib only) |
| `admin/build/gate.py` | The release gate |
| `assets/` | One stylesheet, one script, the icon |
| `lab/shots/` | Phone screenshots from the lab's vaults |
| `findings/img/` | Evidence screenshots attached to findings |

## Build and check

```
python3 admin/build/build.py     # write every generated file
python3 admin/build/gate.py      # must print GATE PASS
python3 -m http.server 8000      # then open http://localhost:8000/
```

## The gate

CI runs it on every push, and a release is the commit it passes on. It fails if:

- any generated file is stale (the build is re-run and compared byte for byte), or any `.html` in the tree is not generated;
- a finding is missing a field, uses an unknown product, area, problem, visibility, recommendation, kind, severity, status or principle, repeats an id, has a date that is not a date, or attaches an image that is missing or has no alt text;
- a principle, problem, visibility or recommendation has no finding that uses it;
- an internal link or `#anchor` on any page goes nowhere, or a page has no markdown twin;
- a colour is written anywhere but the token block at the top of `assets/site.css`;
- the version disagrees between `data/versions.json`, the pages, `llms.txt` and `index.md`;
- a lab screenshot named in `data/lab.json` is missing, or a credential that is not a published read key appears in a tracked file.

## Versions

The version is shown once, in the footer, and links to [what changed](/admin/versions.md).

Each release bumps the last number (v0.4.0 → v0.4.1), unless the project lead asks for a larger step. Every release gets an entry in `data/versions.json` naming what changed and the files it touched.

# Versions

The current version is v0.5.0. Newest first.

## v0.5.0 · 2026-10-28

A redesign to match the rest of the network, and a finder that works like a repo picker: type, the best match is already highlighted, arrows move, Enter opens.

- `assets/site.css`: the network's teal palette and serif headings, light and dark; a sticky header with the part-of-sgit.ai pill, version chip, Search and GitHub buttons; a centred home hero
- `assets/finder.js`: type-ahead over findings, principles, exemplars and pages, on the home page and as a palette from any page (Search button, / or Ctrl/Cmd+K); no JavaScript still means a plain search form and link
- `assets/findings.js`: the nine dropdowns are now behind one filters button with an active-count badge; one search field first, one-tap chips (Open, High severity, Fixed, Failures, Gaps), best title match first, matches highlighted, arrow keys and Enter, a copy-link button
- `assets/search.json`: the type-ahead index, generated by the build so it cannot list what does not exist
- `content/index.md`: the home page lists five high-severity findings rather than sixteen (the same overload UX-002 reports), with a link to the rest; the search field is on the first screen
- `admin/build/build.py`: the {{finder}} and {{quick}} directives, a limit option on {{findings-list}}, the new header and footer

## v0.4.1 · 2026-10-25

Voice input that can throw away your words: four findings on the Claude app's dictation controls, one thing it gets right, and two principles about lost work and silent systems.

- `data/findings.json`: UX-060 (X discards the recording without confirmation), UX-061 (three unlabelled controls), UX-062 (silent second-pass rewrite), UX-063 (live transcript stalls with no state shown), with a screenshot
- `data/exemplars.json`: EX-002, the live transcript as proof the recording is working
- `data/principles.json`: work is never lost to one tap or a silent failure; the reader can always tell what the system is doing
- `data/taxonomy.json`: problem "missing feedback"; recommendations "confirm or undo", "show the state", "show what changed"
- `data/site.json`: the Claude app product covers iPhone and iPad; new area: input and dictation
- `content/admin/index.md`: releases bump the patch number

## v0.4.0 · 2026-10-25

A security prompt that asks for a decision it does not explain: UX-059, and a principle for informed decisions.

- `data/findings.json`: UX-059, the Claude app's Bash permission prompt shows raw, truncated code and no plain-words summary, with a screenshot
- `data/principles.json`: new principle, a decision comes with what you need to make it
- `data/taxonomy.json`: problem "uninformed decision", recommendation "explain the decision"
- `data/site.json`: Claude app on iPhone added as a product (type: app); new area: security decisions

## v0.3.0 · 2026-10-18

What good looks like: exemplars join the register, starting with Safari on iPad, and a principle for interfaces that can be learned.

- `data/exemplars.json + /exemplars/`: EX-001, Safari on iPad collapses its toolbars after a small scroll at any speed; answers UX-057 and UX-058
- `data/principles.json`: new principle, the same gesture gives the same result, so it can be learned; UX-058 moved to it
- `data/site.json`: Safari on iPad added as a product
- Finding pages link the exemplars that answer them; principle sections link the exemplars that demonstrate them; the gate checks exemplars

## v0.2.1 · 2026-10-18

Hiding Firefox's toolbars on an iPad depends on the speed of the flick, so the reader cannot choose it; and three newsroom findings re-checked from a reader's screenshots.

- `data/findings.json`: UX-058 (toolbar state depends on gesture speed) with two screenshots in findings/img/; UX-057 points to it
- `data/findings.json`: UX-003 and UX-004 fixed, UX-028 partly fixed, each re-checked on newsroom v0.12.120
- `data/taxonomy.json`: new problem "unpredictable control" and recommendation "make it predictable"

## v0.2.0 · 2026-10-18

The register is indexed nine ways, and the first reports from readers arrive: two Firefox-on-iPad findings about a page that will not hold still.

- `data/taxonomy.json`: problem (24), visibility (4) and recommendation (17) vocabularies; every existing finding backfilled
- `data/site.json`: sites become products, with a type (site, platform, prototype, browser); Firefox on iPad added
- `data/findings.json`: UX-056 (scroll up focuses the address bar and opens the keyboard) and UX-057 (toolbars return on any scroll up), with screenshots in findings/img/
- `data/principles.json`: new principle, nothing moves that the reader did not move; UX-051 moved to it
- `content/browse/index.md`: every facet with counts, each value a link to the filtered list
- `admin/build/`: facets drive filters, finding pages, browse and llms.txt; the gate checks the taxonomy and evidence images

## v0.1.0 · 2026-10-18

The first release: a register of UX failures and gaps, seeded from the newsroom review, with the review, the design lab and the method it was made by.

- `data/findings.json`: 55 findings (newsroom.sgit.ai, the vault host, and the lab's own prototypes), each with evidence, impact, fix, status and the principle it breaks
- `data/principles.json`: 14 principles, each listing the findings that break it
- `content/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md`: the newsroom UX review of 11 October 2026, published whole
- `content/lab/index.md + lab/shots/`: the Newsroom Design Lab, its four vaults with read keys, and 24 phone screenshots in three directions
- `content/method/index.md`: the reader path, the panel, severity, and how a finding is filed
- `admin/build/`: build.py, md.py and gate.py, stdlib only

/browse/  ·  /browse/index.md
==============================================================================

# Browse the register

The same findings, indexed nine ways. Each value links to the [findings list](/findings/index.md) filtered to it, and filters combine: `/findings/?problem=unexpected-movement&visibility=intermittent` is a link you can send. The vocabularies live in [/data/taxonomy.json](/data/taxonomy.json) and grow only when a finding needs a value that is not there yet.

[Product](#by-product) · [Area](#by-area) · [Problem](#by-problem) · [Visibility](#by-visibility) · [Recommendation](#by-recommendation) · [Principle](#by-principle) · [Severity](#by-severity) · [Status](#by-status) · [Kind](#by-kind)

And the other direction: [what good looks like](/exemplars/index.md), things that work, each linked to the findings it answers.

## By product

Whose fault it is: one of our sites, the platform under them, our own prototypes, or the browser the reader uses.

| Product | Findings | Open | Means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| newsroom.sgit.ai | [45](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai) | 39 | The publication: articles on AI agents, security and publishing, written with an agent newsroom (site) |

| Claude app (iPhone and iPad) | [5](/findings/?product=claude-app-ios) | 5 | The Claude app on iOS and iPadOS, used here to run and supervise Claude Code sessions, often by voice (app) |

## By problem

What kind of thing goes wrong. A finding can have more than one.

| Problem | Findings | Open | Means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Uninformed decision | [2](/findings/?problem=uninformed-decision) | 2 | The reader is asked to decide without what they need to judge it: what it does, what it touches, what could go wrong |
| Missing feedback | [1](/findings/?problem=missing-feedback) | 1 | No sign of what the system is doing, so the reader cannot tell progress from failure |
| Unexpected movement | [4](/findings/?problem=unexpected-movement) | 3 | Part of the interface moves when the reader did not move it |
| Focus hijack | [1](/findings/?problem=focus-hijack) | 1 | Focus or input goes somewhere the reader did not send it |
| Unpredictable control | [1](/findings/?problem=unpredictable-control) | 1 | The result of a gesture depends on something the reader cannot see or control, such as its speed, so the state they want cannot be reached on purpose |
| Lost screen space | [2](/findings/?problem=lost-screen-space) | 2 | Chrome takes screen that the content needed |
| Wrong culprit | [1](/findings/?problem=wrong-culprit) | 1 | The reader blames the wrong party: the page for the browser, the site for the platform |
| Buried content | [4](/findings/?problem=buried-content) | 4 | What the reader came for is pushed down or out of view |
| Overload | [4](/findings/?problem=overload) | 4 | Too much at once, so nothing is chosen for the reader |
| Builder chrome | [5](/findings/?problem=builder-chrome) | 5 | Things for the author, an agent or the build, shown to readers |
| Missing signal | [10](/findings/?problem=missing-signal) | 9 | The reader lacks what they need to decide: length, format, who wrote it, whether it is real |
| Missing way in | [4](/findings/?problem=missing-way-in) | 3 | A page or path the reader needs does not exist |
| Dead end | [6](/findings/?problem=dead-end) | 5 | Something that looks like a way in goes nowhere |
| Unshareable view | [2](/findings/?problem=unshareable-view) | 2 | A view the reader can see but cannot link to |
| Unlabelled | [5](/findings/?problem=unlabelled) | 5 | A number, value or control with no label |
| Alarming wording | [3](/findings/?problem=alarming-wording) | 2 | Words that read as a threat, a debt or a trick when they describe something benign |
| Silent change | [2](/findings/?problem=silent-change) | 2 | State changes without telling the reader |
| Preselected input | [1](/findings/?problem=preselected-input) | 1 | An answer is chosen before the reader chooses |
| Unconsented state | [2](/findings/?problem=unconsented-state) | 2 | Something is kept or added because the reader opened something |
| Missing channel | [3](/findings/?problem=missing-channel) | 3 | No way for the reader to reach a person |
| Inconsistent facts | [5](/findings/?problem=inconsistent-facts) | 3 | Two places disagree about the same fact |
| Stale claim | [2](/findings/?problem=stale-claim) | 1 | A statement about the present that is no longer true |
| Hidden until script | [2](/findings/?problem=hidden-until-script) | 2 | Content appears only after scripts or prior state |
| Host trap | [4](/findings/?problem=host-trap) | 4 | The platform behaves unlike a normal page, and the difference is not visible |
| Data loss | [4](/findings/?problem=data-loss) | 4 | Something the reader made or kept is lost or cut |
| Layout overflow | [1](/findings/?problem=layout-overflow) | 0 | Content wider or taller than the screen it is on |
| Untested path | [1](/findings/?problem=untested-path) | 1 | A path shown to readers that nobody has seen work |

## By visibility

How the reader experiences it: seen every time, sometimes, only felt, or not at all.

| Visibility | Findings | Open | Means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Obvious | [18](/findings/?visibility=obvious) | 14 | Every reader sees it, every time they reach that point |
| Intermittent | [7](/findings/?visibility=intermittent) | 7 | Some readers, some of the time: depends on a gesture, a device or a state, and is hard to reproduce on demand |
| Subtle | [22](/findings/?visibility=subtle) | 20 | Felt more than seen: it costs attention or trust, but is not noticed as a bug |
| Silent | [16](/findings/?visibility=silent) | 14 | No symptom on screen: found only by measuring, or by its consequences |

## By recommendation

The shape of the fix. Findings with the same recommendation are often fixed by the same change.

| Recommendation | Findings | Open | Means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Explain the decision | [1](/findings/?recommendation=explain-the-decision) | 1 | Before asking, say in plain words what will happen, what it touches, whether it can be undone and why it is being asked, with the raw detail one tap away |
| Confirm or undo | [1](/findings/?recommendation=confirm-or-undo) | 1 | A destructive action either asks first or can be undone, and the safe choice is the easy one |
| Show the state | [1](/findings/?recommendation=show-the-state) | 1 | Always show what the system is doing (listening, working, paused, failed) and keep what was captured until it is safely delivered |
| Show what changed | [1](/findings/?recommendation=show-what-changed) | 1 | When the system rewrites what the reader made, mark it, and let them see and undo the change |
| Keep the UI still | [3](/findings/?recommendation=keep-the-ui-still) | 2 | Nothing moves, appears or takes focus unless the reader asked for it; chrome that hides stays hidden until a deliberate gesture |
| Make it predictable | [1](/findings/?recommendation=make-it-predictable) | 1 | The same gesture always gives the same result, and the reader can set the state directly instead of coaxing it |
| Cut to the essential | [3](/findings/?recommendation=cut-to-the-essential) | 3 | Remove or move down everything that is not the lead, the doors and the next step |
| Write for a stranger | [1](/findings/?recommendation=write-for-a-stranger) | 1 | Rewrite the words for someone arriving for the first time |
| Show it up front | [7](/findings/?recommendation=show-it-up-front) | 6 | Put the signal the reader decides by (length, author, short version, real numbers) where they look first |
| Say what it is | [8](/findings/?recommendation=say-what-it-is) | 7 | Label it, in the reader's terms, at the moment it matters |
| Start empty | [1](/findings/?recommendation=start-empty) | 1 | Inputs start unselected; record only what the reader did |
| Ask first | [2](/findings/?recommendation=ask-first) | 2 | Make keeping, adding or following a tap the reader makes |
| Make it a link | [2](/findings/?recommendation=make-it-a-link) | 2 | Give the view, filter or label an address, and make it go there |
| Build the way in | [8](/findings/?recommendation=build-the-way-in) | 7 | Create the missing page or path: tag pages, series, start here, a branded 404 |
| Open a channel | [3](/findings/?recommendation=open-a-channel) | 3 | Send it to a person by default, with consent, and give the reader a receipt |
| Generate from one source | [4](/findings/?recommendation=generate-from-one-source) | 3 | Publish once and generate every copy, count and label from one manifest |
| Check it at build | [3](/findings/?recommendation=check-at-build) | 1 | Make the release fail when it happens again |
| Move it to the workshop | [4](/findings/?recommendation=move-to-the-workshop) | 4 | Take builder things off reader pages, one link away |
| Render on the first load | [2](/findings/?recommendation=render-on-first-load) | 2 | Show the content in the HTML, with no scripts and no prior visit needed |
| Date the claim | [2](/findings/?recommendation=date-the-claim) | 1 | Generate or date every statement about now, and mark fixes with their version |
| Design for the host | [4](/findings/?recommendation=design-for-the-host) | 4 | Use the host's own mechanisms (route variable, sg.state, vault snapshot) instead of the browser's defaults |
| Test where readers are | [1](/findings/?recommendation=test-where-readers-are) | 1 | Run it on the device, browser and host readers actually use before showing it |

## By principle

The rule it breaks. Each principle has a one-minute test on the principles page.

| Principle | Findings | Open | Means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A decision comes with what you need to make it | [2](/findings/?principle=informed-decisions) | 2 | Any prompt that asks the reader to decide (allow, pay, share, delete) first says, in plain words, what will happen, what it touches, whether it can be undone, and why it is being asked. The raw detail is there for checking, not as the explanation. |
| Work is never lost to one tap or a silent failure | [1](/findings/?principle=work-is-never-lost) | 1 | What the reader has made (a recording, a draft, a note) cannot be destroyed by a single unlabelled tap, and is kept when something fails. Destructive actions ask first or can be undone; failures keep the raw capture and offer a retry. |
| The reader can always tell what the system is doing | [1](/findings/?principle=system-state-is-visible) | 1 | At every moment the interface shows whether it is listening, working, paused, done or failed. A process that stops shows that it stopped; it never just goes quiet. |
| The first screen is for a stranger | [8](/findings/?principle=stranger-first-screen) | 6 | On a phone, the first screen says what this is, who it is for, and where to go next. The lead is on it. Chrome, metadata and method come after. |
| Nothing moves that the reader did not move | [3](/findings/?principle=ui-stays-still) | 2 | While the reader is reading, the interface holds still. Toolbars, keyboards, banners and panels appear, move or take focus only on a deliberate gesture made for that purpose, never as a side effect of scrolling or reading. |
| The same gesture gives the same result, so it can be learned | [1](/findings/?principle=same-gesture-same-result) | 1 | Every interaction behaves the same way every time, triggered by something the reader controls (where they tap, how far they scroll), never by something they cannot see or repeat (how fast they flicked, what state an animation was in). |
| Label the money, and never surprise with a charge | [5](/findings/?principle=label-the-money) | 4 | Every number that is money says what it is. The first time anything is charged, the reader is told before or as it happens. Wording about balances never reads as debt or threat. |
| A default is not an answer | [2](/findings/?principle=defaults-are-not-answers) | 2 | Inputs that ask the reader's opinion start empty. Only what the reader actually did is recorded. |
| Ask before keeping | [2](/findings/?principle=ask-before-keeping) | 2 | Nothing is added to the reader's lists, profile or storage because they opened something. Keeping is a tap the reader makes. |
| Every view is a link | [4](/findings/?principle=every-view-is-a-link) | 3 | Anything a reader can see, they can send: a filter, a search, a tag, a desk, a part of a series. The address changes when the view does. |
| No dead ends | [7](/findings/?principle=no-dead-ends) | 6 | Everything that looks like a way in is one: tags link to pages, missing pages offer the way back, each article ends with one next step. |
| One source of truth for every fact | [4](/findings/?principle=one-source-of-truth) | 3 | Each piece of content is published once, at one canonical address. Every count, date and label is generated from one manifest at build time. |
| The publication is not the workshop | [4](/findings/?principle=publication-not-workshop) | 4 | Reader pages carry reader things. How the site is built (versions, author tooling, agent strips, release history, admin) lives in one clearly separate area, one link away. |
| Feedback reaches someone, and the reader gets a receipt | [3](/findings/?principle=feedback-reaches-someone) | 3 | Every rating, request or 'what is missing' goes somewhere a person reads it, by default and with plain consent, and the reader keeps a receipt of what was sent. |
| Say how long, and what kind, before the reader commits | [3](/findings/?principle=length-before-commitment) | 3 | Every card and every link to a long piece shows reading time and format. Every long piece opens with a short version. |
| Say who wrote it, and how | [4](/findings/?principle=say-who-wrote-it) | 4 | The byline names the person and the way the piece was made (with agents, from voice notes), where the reader looks, not in the footer. The purpose of the publication is one link away. |
| Content is visible without waiting for scripts | [2](/findings/?principle=content-is-visible) | 2 | The page renders its content in HTML and shows it at once. Scripts enhance; they never gate what the reader can see. |
| What a page says about the present is true now | [4](/findings/?principle=state-is-current) | 3 | Labels like 'edition of', 'currently', 'broken' and 'live' are dated or generated, and change when the facts do. A fixed problem is marked fixed, with the version. |
| A vault app works inside the host, not just on its own | [3](/findings/?principle=host-safe-apps) | 3 | An app is tested where readers open it: inside the vault host's sandboxed frame. Routing never assigns location.hash, storage goes through the host, and network reads come from the vault. |

## By severity

High loses the reader or their trust on the first visit; medium costs effort or a return; low is polish.

| Severity | Findings | Open | Means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| High | [20](/findings/?severity=high) | 16 |  |
| Medium | [25](/findings/?severity=medium) | 21 |  |
| Low | [18](/findings/?severity=low) | 18 |  |

A failure works against the reader; a gap is something they need that is not there.

| Kind | Findings | Open | Means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Failure | [44](/findings/?kind=failure) | 38 | Something works against the reader |
| Gap | [19](/findings/?kind=gap) | 17 | Something the reader needs is not there |

/exemplars/EX-001.html  ·  /exemplars/EX-001.md

[What good looks like](/exemplars/index.md) / EX-001

# Safari on iPad hides its toolbars the same way every time, after a small scroll

## What it does

At the top of a page Safari shows its full toolbars: sidebar, back, address field, share, new tab, tabs, and a tab strip (first screenshot; the page starts about 270 px down a 1,640 px screen). Any small scroll down, slow or fast, collapses them to a small address pill (second screenshot; the page starts about 120 px down). Here the page had moved by only a couple of lines of breadcrumb: the article title is still where it was.

![Safari on iPad at the top of a newsroom article: sidebar, back, address field, share, new tab and tabs buttons, and a tab strip above the page](/exemplars/img/EX-001-safari-at-top.webp)

_At the top: the full toolbars and the tab strip._

![The same article after a small scroll: Safari shows only a small address pill, and the article title is still on screen](/exemplars/img/EX-001-safari-after-small-scroll.webp)

_After a small scroll, at any speed: a small address pill. The page has moved by two lines._

## Why it works

It is predictable. The trigger is a small distance scrolled, which the reader controls, not the speed of the gesture, so it behaves the same every time and is learned after one or two uses. The collapsed state is small enough to be a fair trade for the space, and getting there costs only a couple of lines of scroll, so the reader never loses their place to reach it.

## What it still does not do

It still moves the page: the toolbars collapse as a side effect of scrolling, and the reader would prefer them to stay collapsed without having to move anything. It is a good compromise, not the ideal.

## The findings it answers

- [UX-058 Whether the toolbars hide depends on how fast you scroll, not how far](/findings/UX-058.md)
- [UX-057 The toolbars come back on any small scroll up, taking screen and moving the page](/findings/UX-057.md)

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Product** | [Safari on iPad](https://www.apple.com/safari/), browser |
| **Where** | https://newsroom.sgit.ai/ (an article page, newsroom v0.12.106) |
| **Environment** | Safari on an iPad, landscape |
| **Demonstrates** | [The same gesture gives the same result, so it can be learned](/principles/index.md#same-gesture-same-result) |
| **Recommendation** | [Make it predictable](/findings/?recommendation=make-it-predictable) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-18, not recorded |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-18, not recorded |
| **Source** | [Reported by Dinis Cruz, 18 Oct 2026, with screenshots](/method/index.md#reports-from-readers) |

/exemplars/EX-002.html  ·  /exemplars/EX-002.md

[What good looks like](/exemplars/index.md) / EX-002

# Dictation that shows your words as you speak them

## What it does

While you dictate, the Claude app writes the transcript into the message box as you speak, then refines it in a second pass when you stop. The first pass is rough, but it is immediate.

## Why it works

Seeing your words appear is proof that they are being captured. It is the reason the reporter uses this input over others: as long as the text keeps appearing, they know the recording is safe, and they can keep their attention on what they are saying.

## What it still does not do

When the live pass stalls (UX-063), the proof disappears with no explanation, and the second pass rewrites text without showing what changed (UX-062). The feedback is the right idea; it needs to cover the failure cases too.

## The findings it answers

- [UX-063 The live transcript sometimes stops while you are still speaking, and nothing says whether it is still recording](/findings/UX-063.md)

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Product** | [Claude app (iPhone and iPad)](https://claude.ai/download), app |
| **Where** | Message box, voice input |
| **Environment** | Claude app on iPad, landscape, dictating a message into a Claude Code session |
| **Demonstrates** | [The reader can always tell what the system is doing](/principles/index.md#system-state-is-visible) |
| **Recommendation** | [Show the state](/findings/?recommendation=show-the-state) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-25, not recorded |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-25, not recorded |
| **Source** | [Reported by Dinis Cruz, 25 Oct 2026, by voice, with a screenshot](/method/index.md#reports-from-readers) |

/exemplars/  ·  /exemplars/index.md

# What good looks like

A finding says what is wrong; an exemplar shows something that already gets it right, so a fix can point at a working example instead of a description. Each one is measured like a finding (where, when, on what device), says **why** it works, and says honestly what it still does not do. They come from anywhere: our own sites, other sites, browsers, apps.

- [EX-001](/exemplars/EX-001.md) · Safari on iPad · Safari on iPad hides its toolbars the same way every time, after a small scroll (answers UX-058, UX-057)
- [EX-002](/exemplars/EX-002.md) · Claude app (iPhone and iPad) · Dictation that shows your words as you speak them (answers UX-063)

Each exemplar is linked from the findings it answers, and from the [principle](/principles/index.md) it demonstrates. The source is [/data/exemplars.json](/data/exemplars.json).

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-001

# The first phone screen explains how the site is built, not what it is about

Open · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

At 390×844 the first screen holds a two-row header, a "For agents /llms.txt" strip, three lines of metadata, a tagline about method, a second navigation bar and an editor's note. The lead story starts on screen two.

## Why it matters

A contact who taps a link cannot tell in one screen that this is a publication about AI agents, security and publishing, or why they were sent it.

## The fix

One sentence on what this is, who writes it, three doors (security, builders, news) and the lead, all on screen one. Everything else moves below or into the menu.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/> |
| **Problems** | [Buried content](/findings/?problem=buried-content), [Builder chrome](/findings/?problem=builder-chrome) |
| **Visibility** | [Obvious](/findings/?visibility=obvious): every reader sees it, every time they reach that point |
| **Recommendation** | [Cut to the essential](/findings/?recommendation=cut-to-the-essential): remove or move down everything that is not the lead, the doors and the next step |
| **Area** | [First visit](/findings/?area=first-visit) |
| **Breaks** | [The first screen is for a stranger](/principles/index.md#stranger-first-screen) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-002

# The home page is 59 phone screens long, with 845 links

Open · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The phone home page measures 49,715 px: Latest, Highlights, desk notes, collections, the full article list, then a map of every article's links.

## Why it matters

The front page tries to show everything, so it chooses nothing for the reader. Nobody scrolls 59 screens; the curation is invisible.

## The fix

Cut the home page to the lead, three per desk, collections and the newsletter. Lists and the link map move to their own pages.

## The record

| **Visibility** | [Obvious](/findings/?visibility=obvious): every reader sees it, every time they reach that point |
| **Recommendation** | [Cut to the essential](/findings/?recommendation=cut-to-the-essential): remove or move down everything that is not the lead, the doors and the next step |
| **Area** | [First visit](/findings/?area=first-visit) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-003

# The masthead line describes a method, not a subject

Fixed · medium severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The tagline is "one page, one argument, with the figures, the data and the links to check it". Nothing says agents, AI governance, security or news economics.

## Why it matters

The one line every visitor reads tells them how the site works instead of what it is about.

## The fix

A masthead line that names the subject and the author, e.g. "Field notes on AI agents, security and the next generation of publishing, by Dinis Cruz".

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Fixed. Fixed by v0.12.120: the masthead now reads "Field notes on AI agents, security and the next generation of publishing, by Dinis Cruz" (the lab's first candidate). Seen at iPad width, 18 Oct. |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Gap: something the reader needs is not there |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/> |
| **Problems** | [Missing signal](/findings/?problem=missing-signal) |
| **Visibility** | [Subtle](/findings/?visibility=subtle): felt more than seen: it costs attention or trust, but is not noticed as a bug |
| **Recommendation** | [Show it up front](/findings/?recommendation=show-it-up-front): put the signal the reader decides by (length, author, short version, real numbers) where they look first |
| **Area** | [First visit](/findings/?area=first-visit) |
| **Breaks** | [The first screen is for a stranger](/principles/index.md#stranger-first-screen) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-18, v0.12.120 |
| **Source** | [Review: the direction](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#the-direction-a-publication-with-a-heart) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-004

# The edition label is older than the articles under it

Fixed · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The home page says "Edition of 2026-10-08" above ten articles dated 10 October. Still the case in v0.7.1, above articles from 10 and 11 October.

## Why it matters

A front page that looks three days stale on the day it was published tells a reader the site is not kept.

## The fix

Date the edition from the newest article at build time, or label it as the editor's pick of its date.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Fixed. Fixed by v0.12.120: "Edition of 18 October 2026" above articles dated 18 October. Seen at iPad width, 18 Oct. |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/> |
| **Problems** | [Stale claim](/findings/?problem=stale-claim) |
| **Visibility** | [Subtle](/findings/?visibility=subtle): felt more than seen: it costs attention or trust, but is not noticed as a bug |
| **Recommendation** | [Date the claim](/findings/?recommendation=date-the-claim): generate or date every statement about now, and mark fixes with their version |
| **Area** | [First visit](/findings/?area=first-visit) |
| **Breaks** | [What a page says about the present is true now](/principles/index.md#state-is-current) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-18, v0.12.120 |

# The version number is shown three times on the first screen

Open · low severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

v0.7.1 appears three times on the desktop first screen: in the agent strip, the metadata lines and the footer badge.

## Why it matters

# A "For agents /llms.txt" strip sits above the masthead

Open · low severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The first element on every page is a strip addressed to agents, above the publication's name.

## Why it matters

Useful to agents, noise to a person, and it takes the most valuable line on the screen.

## The fix

Move it to the page head (link rel) and the footer, where agents look anyway. Satisfies both the Architect and the Designer on the panel.

# The editor's note is written for someone who read the last two editions

Open · low severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

## Why it matters

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-008

# Content is hidden until JavaScript runs

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The body starts at opacity 0 and only appears when a "ready" class is added, with a 1.6 s fallback.

## Why it matters

On a slow phone, or for any reader or agent that does not run the script, the page is blank.

## The fix

Render visible by default; animate only enhancements.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/> |
| **Problems** | [Hidden until script](/findings/?problem=hidden-until-script) |
| **Visibility** | [Intermittent](/findings/?visibility=intermittent): some readers, some of the time: depends on a gesture, a device or a state, and is hard to reproduce on demand |
| **Recommendation** | [Render on the first load](/findings/?recommendation=render-on-first-load): show the content in the HTML, with no scripts and no prior visit needed |
| **Area** | [Trust](/findings/?area=trust) |
| **Breaks** | [Content is visible without waiting for scripts](/principles/index.md#content-is-visible) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: bugs and broken things](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#bugs-and-broken-things) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-009

# Two navigation bars, and a 60-link menu that mixes reading with building

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

A second bar of nine links repeats the menu. The menu holds about 60 links in nine groups (57 links in 8 groups when the lab mapped it), mixing reader pages (Newsletter, Collections) with builder pages (Replicate, Admin, Release history, The run log).

## Why it matters

The reader has to sort the publication from the workshop themselves, twice.

## The fix

One navigation. The publication on top; the workshop behind one item with its own front page.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |

| **Visibility** | [Obvious](/findings/?visibility=obvious): every reader sees it, every time they reach that point |
| **Recommendation** | [Move it to the workshop](/findings/?recommendation=move-to-the-workshop): take builder things off reader pages, one link away |
| **Area** | [Navigation](/findings/?area=navigation) |
| **Breaks** | [The publication is not the workshop](/principles/index.md#publication-not-workshop) |

# Missing pages show the default GitHub Pages 404

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

Any missing URL shows GitHub's generic error page, with no link back to the newsroom.

## Why it matters

A mistyped or old link ends the visit on a page that does not even say which site it is.

## The fix

A branded 404.html with search and the three entry doors.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |

| **Recommendation** | [Build the way in](/findings/?recommendation=build-the-way-in): create the missing page or path: tag pages, series, start here, a branded 404 |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-011

# Links without extensions in one article

Open · low severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

future-of-news links to /thesis, /portugal and /economics/rails, unlike every other link on the site.

## Why it matters

They depend on the host resolving extensionless paths; on a strict host or a mirror they break.

## The fix

Use the full .html or trailing-slash form everywhere; check it at build.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Low |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/future-of-news-story-vault-not-paywall.html> |
| **Problems** | [Dead end](/findings/?problem=dead-end) |
| **Visibility** | [Silent](/findings/?visibility=silent): no symptom on screen: found only by measuring, or by its consequences |
| **Recommendation** | [Check it at build](/findings/?recommendation=check-at-build): make the release fail when it happens again |
| **Area** | [Navigation](/findings/?area=navigation) |
| **Breaks** | [No dead ends](/principles/index.md#no-dead-ends) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-012

# Each article ends with seven next steps instead of one

Open · low severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

After the rating scales the foot of an article offers many routes onward with equal weight.

## Why it matters

At the moment the reader is most ready to continue, the page makes them choose among seven.

## The fix

One next step: the next part of the series, or the next "start here" piece for the reader's desk, then the newsletter.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Low |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/> |
| **Problems** | [Overload](/findings/?problem=overload) |
| **Visibility** | [Subtle](/findings/?visibility=subtle): felt more than seen: it costs attention or trust, but is not noticed as a bug |
| **Recommendation** | [Cut to the essential](/findings/?recommendation=cut-to-the-essential): remove or move down everything that is not the lead, the doors and the next step |
| **Area** | [Navigation](/findings/?area=navigation) |
| **Breaks** | [No dead ends](/principles/index.md#no-dead-ends) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-013

# One topic holds more than half the articles

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

"Agents & policy" holds 35 of 67 articles (38 of 73 in the lab's snapshot). The other five topics hold 13 to 26 and overlap: an article sits in about two.

## Why it matters

A CISO who picks the obvious topic still faces 35 long reads. The classification does not help anyone choose.

## The fix

Desks by audience, not internal topic: security, building, vaults, news, strategy (18 / 17 / 14 / 15 / 9 in the lab).

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/> |
| **Problems** | [Overload](/findings/?problem=overload) |
| **Visibility** | [Subtle](/findings/?visibility=subtle): felt more than seen: it costs attention or trust, but is not noticed as a bug |
| **Recommendation** | [Build the way in](/findings/?recommendation=build-the-way-in): create the missing page or path: tag pages, series, start here, a branded 404 |
| **Area** | [Findability](/findings/?area=findability) |
| **Breaks** | [Every view is a link](/principles/index.md#every-view-is-a-link) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: findability](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#findability-and-information-architecture) |
| **Prototype** | [Findability](/lab/index.md#newsroom-proto-find), route `desks`, in three directions |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-014

# Tags are not links, and there are no tag pages

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The lead article carries 12 tag pills; none links anywhere. Tags mix subjects, formats and product names ("article", "riskmandate"). 339 raw tags, 228 used once.

## Why it matters

The most precise way into the archive looks clickable and goes nowhere.

## The fix

A controlled vocabulary of about 40 tags owned by the Librarian, a page per tag, tags as links capped at five per article (339 → 42 in the lab; median 11 → 4).

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/hope-or-enforcement.html> |
| **Problems** | [Dead end](/findings/?problem=dead-end) |
| **Visibility** | [Obvious](/findings/?visibility=obvious): every reader sees it, every time they reach that point |
| **Recommendation** | [Make it a link](/findings/?recommendation=make-it-a-link): give the view, filter or label an address, and make it go there |
| **Area** | [Findability](/findings/?area=findability) |
| **Breaks** | [No dead ends](/principles/index.md#no-dead-ends) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: findability](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#findability-and-information-architecture) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-015

# Filters cannot be shared

Open · medium severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

Choosing a topic on the article list does not change the address.

## Why it matters

You cannot send a contact "the security articles"; you can only send the whole list and an instruction.

## The fix

Put every filter in the address (/articles/?desk=security, or in the path where query strings are not allowed).

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Gap: something the reader needs is not there |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/> |
| **Problems** | [Unshareable view](/findings/?problem=unshareable-view) |
| **Visibility** | [Silent](/findings/?visibility=silent): no symptom on screen: found only by measuring, or by its consequences |
| **Recommendation** | [Make it a link](/findings/?recommendation=make-it-a-link): give the view, filter or label an address, and make it go there |
| **Area** | [Findability](/findings/?area=findability) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-016

# Series are invisible

Open · medium severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The reading meter in five pieces, the homepage diagnosis and its rebuild, the agent team in three depths: nothing says "part 2 of 5" or offers the next part. The lab found eleven series.

## Why it matters

Readers land in the middle of a story without knowing there is a beginning.

## The fix

Series pages with part numbers, previous / next on each part, and the reader's progress.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |

| **Recommendation** | [Build the way in](/findings/?recommendation=build-the-way-in): create the missing page or path: tag pages, series, start here, a branded 404 |
| **Area** | [Findability](/findings/?area=findability) |
| **Breaks** | [No dead ends](/principles/index.md#no-dead-ends) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-017

# There is no "start here" path

Open · medium severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The Historian's weekly note and the collections are the best orientation on the site, and they sit below the fold.

## Why it matters

A newcomer facing 73 long articles has no way to know which five to read first.

## The fix

Each desk opens with "Start here: five articles in order", written by the Historian.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Gap: something the reader needs is not there |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/> |
| **Problems** | [Missing way in](/findings/?problem=missing-way-in) |
| **Visibility** | [Subtle](/findings/?visibility=subtle): felt more than seen: it costs attention or trust, but is not noticed as a bug |
| **Recommendation** | [Build the way in](/findings/?recommendation=build-the-way-in): create the missing page or path: tag pages, series, start here, a branded 404 |
| **Area** | [Findability](/findings/?area=findability) |
| **Breaks** | [The first screen is for a stranger](/principles/index.md#stranger-first-screen) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: findability](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#findability-and-information-architecture) |
| **Prototype** | [Findability](/lab/index.md#newsroom-proto-find), route `desk/security`, in three directions |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-018

# Cards do not show reading time or format

Open · medium severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The median article is about 4,500 words and 25 of 66 are over 5,000, yet no card shows reading time or whether it is a field report, explainer, analysis or desk note.

## Why it matters

A reader with three minutes cannot tell a note from a 40-minute analysis before opening it.

## The fix

Reading time and a format label on every card, derived at build.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |

# Search only matches titles, teasers and tags

Open · low severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The search box does not look inside articles, although a markdown twin of every article exists.

## Why it matters

About 300,000 words are unsearchable; a reader who remembers a phrase cannot find the piece.

Search over bodies and abstracts from the markdown twins, with snippets.

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-020

# The best reader feature is buried under metadata and a long italic abstract

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

On the lead article (about 8,000 words) a phone reader scrolls past a three-line breadcrumb, a byline with two version numbers, 12 tag pills and a 250-word italic abstract before reaching the "Five readers" block.

## Why it matters

The short version that would let a reader decide is found only by those who already decided to read.

## The fix

Title and standfirst; a byline that says how it was made, date and reading time; the short version in three or four sentences; reader views as one row; then the article. Tags and versions to the foot.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/hope-or-enforcement.html> |
| **Problems** | [Buried content](/findings/?problem=buried-content) |
| **Visibility** | [Obvious](/findings/?visibility=obvious): every reader sees it, every time they reach that point |
| **Recommendation** | [Show it up front](/findings/?recommendation=show-it-up-front): put the signal the reader decides by (length, author, short version, real numbers) where they look first |
| **Area** | [Article page](/findings/?area=article) |
| **Breaks** | [Say how long, and what kind, before the reader commits](/principles/index.md#length-before-commitment) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: article page and feedback](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#article-page-and-feedback) |
| **Prototype** | [Article & reader primitives](/lab/index.md#newsroom-proto-article), route `article/hope-or-enforcement`, in three directions |

# Author tooling is shown to every reader

Open · low severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

Every article ends with "Posting this article on LinkedIn?" and the cover image's filename.

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-022

# The byline names one human; the AI authorship is in the footer

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

Articles are written from voice notes by a desk of named agents; the byline says only "Dinis Cruz" and the agent newsroom is credited in the footer.

## Why it matters

A reader who finds the disclosure late reads it as something hidden, on a publication whose pitch is provenance.

## The fix

"Dinis Cruz, written with the SGit agent newsroom" in the byline, linked to the purpose page.

## The record

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-023

# There is no page that says why the publication exists

Open · medium severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The agenda (build sgit.ai and RiskMandate, which most articles use as evidence), the licences and the participant disclosure are spread across the footer and method pages.

## Why it matters

Readers cannot judge the argument without knowing who is making it and why.

## The fix

A purpose page, linked from the masthead and every byline: the agenda, open by default, how it is written, who it is for, what I want from you.

## The record

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-024

# All three rating scales start on 3

Open · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The usefulness, more-like-this and level-of-detail scales at the foot of every article are preselected on the middle value.

## Why it matters

Neither the reader nor the author can tell "not rated" from "useful". Every rating collected so far is ambiguous.

## The fix

Start unselected; record only real taps.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/> |
| **Problems** | [Preselected input](/findings/?problem=preselected-input) |
| **Visibility** | [Subtle](/findings/?visibility=subtle): felt more than seen: it costs attention or trust, but is not noticed as a bug |
| **Recommendation** | [Start empty](/findings/?recommendation=start-empty): inputs start unselected; record only what the reader did |
| **Area** | [Feedback](/findings/?area=feedback) |
| **Breaks** | [A default is not an answer](/principles/index.md#defaults-are-not-answers) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: article page and feedback](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#article-page-and-feedback) |
| **Prototype** | [Article & reader primitives](/lab/index.md#newsroom-proto-article), route `feedback`, in three directions |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-025

# Ratings never reach the author

Open · high severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

Ratings stay in the reader's browser unless they choose to send their whole reading record.

## Why it matters

The first contacts sent to the site teach the author nothing about what landed.

## The fix

One-tap send by default, with plain consent ("Send this rating to Dinis, anonymous"), through the encrypted append lane, with a local receipt.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Gap: something the reader needs is not there |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/> |
| **Problems** | [Missing channel](/findings/?problem=missing-channel) |
| **Visibility** | [Silent](/findings/?visibility=silent): no symptom on screen: found only by measuring, or by its consequences |
| **Recommendation** | [Open a channel](/findings/?recommendation=open-a-channel): send it to a person by default, with consent, and give the reader a receipt |
| **Area** | [Feedback](/findings/?area=feedback) |
| **Breaks** | [Feedback reaches someone, and the reader gets a receipt](/principles/index.md#feedback-reaches-someone) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-026

# There is no way to say what was missing

Open · low severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

Feedback is three scales and nothing else: no free text, no "write about this", no "I need a new version".

## Why it matters

Scores say what, not why. Requests that would become the next pitches have no channel.

## The fix

One optional line ("What would have made this more useful?") and request buttons, sent through the append lane with a receipt.

## The record

# Articles join the reader's list without being asked

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

Opening an article adds it to the reader's reading list automatically.

## Why it matters

The list stops meaning "what I chose to keep" and becomes a history the reader did not ask for.

## The fix

Make "Keep" a tap.

# The £5.00 balance chip has no label

Partly fixed · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

## The fix

Label it "£5 free reading credit".

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-029

# Opening an article charges a penny with no notice

Open · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The chip changes from £5.00 to £4.99 on opening any article, silently. In the synthetic-user study this exact moment made a retired reader ask whether she owed money.

## Why it matters

The first thing a new reader learns about the reading meter is that their balance dropped without being told.

## The fix

Announce the first charge once, in words, at the moment it happens.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/> |
| **Problems** | [Silent change](/findings/?problem=silent-change), [Unlabelled](/findings/?problem=unlabelled) |
| **Visibility** | [Subtle](/findings/?visibility=subtle): felt more than seen: it costs attention or trust, but is not noticed as a bug |
| **Recommendation** | [Say what it is](/findings/?recommendation=say-what-it-is): label it, in the reader's terms, at the moment it matters |
| **Area** | [Money](/findings/?area=money) |
| **Breaks** | [Label the money, and never surprise with a charge](/principles/index.md#label-the-money) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: first visit](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#first-visit-a-contact-arriving-from-a-link) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-030

# "Credit can go below zero" reads as a debt

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The account page says credit can go below zero.

## Why it matters

Readers hear "you can owe us money", on a site that has not asked them for any.

## The fix

Say what actually happens when the free credit is used up, in reader terms.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | Medium |

# "You pay the price" reads as a warning

Open · low severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The caption under the usefulness scale reads "You pay the price".

## Why it matters

# It is unclear how a writer gets paid

Open · high severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

The site states nothing is paid upstream yet, and does not say what will be. A blocking finding of the synthetic-user study.

## Why it matters

# The top-up page said "simulated" while asking for money

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-036

# Articles were published on two domains, and diverged

Fixed · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

sgit.ai/articles/ served five 11 October articles (e.g. no-server-by-design, the-agent-is-the-reader) that returned 404 on newsroom.sgit.ai.

## Why it matters

The same publication was more complete on the wrong site.

## The fix

Publish once to the newsroom; make sgit.ai link or redirect there.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Fixed. Fixed in v0.7.1: all six 11 October articles are live on the newsroom; the count is 73. |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://sgit.ai/articles/> |
| **Problems** | [Inconsistent facts](/findings/?problem=inconsistent-facts) |
| **Visibility** | [Silent](/findings/?visibility=silent): no symptom on screen: found only by measuring, or by its consequences |
| **Recommendation** | [Generate from one source](/findings/?recommendation=generate-from-one-source): publish once and generate every copy, count and label from one manifest |
| **Area** | [Consistency](/findings/?area=consistency) |
| **Breaks** | [One source of truth for every fact](/principles/index.md#one-source-of-truth) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Source** | [Review: bugs and broken things](/reviews/newsroom-2026-10-11.md#bugs-and-broken-things) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-037

# Two domains claim to be canonical for the same article

Open · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

sgit.ai/articles/hope-or-enforcement.html declares canonical sgit.ai; the newsroom copy declares canonical newsroom.sgit.ai.

## Why it matters

Search engines split the article's standing between two copies, and readers can land on either.

## The fix

One canonical, the newsroom; a 301 or a canonical pointing there from sgit.ai.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |

| **Problems** | [Inconsistent facts](/findings/?problem=inconsistent-facts) |
| **Visibility** | [Silent](/findings/?visibility=silent): no symptom on screen: found only by measuring, or by its consequences |
| **Recommendation** | [Generate from one source](/findings/?recommendation=generate-from-one-source): publish once and generate every copy, count and label from one manifest |
| **Area** | [Consistency](/findings/?area=consistency) |
| **Breaks** | [One source of truth for every fact](/principles/index.md#one-source-of-truth) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-038

# Three different article counts

Open · medium severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

sgit.ai said 72, the newsroom home said 67, llms.txt said 66, on the same day.

## Why it matters

When a site cannot count itself, the reader doubts every other number on it.

## The fix

Generate every count from one manifest at build, and fail the release if any page disagrees.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open. wire.json says 73 in v0.7.1; the three surfaces were not re-compared. |
| **Severity** | Medium |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |

| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/> |
| **Problems** | [Inconsistent facts](/findings/?problem=inconsistent-facts) |
| **Visibility** | [Subtle](/findings/?visibility=subtle): felt more than seen: it costs attention or trust, but is not noticed as a bug |
| **Recommendation** | [Generate from one source](/findings/?recommendation=generate-from-one-source): publish once and generate every copy, count and label from one manifest |
| **Area** | [Consistency](/findings/?area=consistency) |
| **Breaks** | [One source of truth for every fact](/principles/index.md#one-source-of-truth) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.6.4 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-044

# The founder page says "the picks above" and no picks render on a phone

Open · high severity · failure · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

On a phone with no prior visit, the founder persona page refers to picks that are not shown.

## Why it matters

The page a founder is sent to points at content that is not there, on the first visit, which is the only one that matters.

## The fix

Render the picks on the landing view with no prior state; test it in a fresh browser.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Product** | [newsroom.sgit.ai](/findings/?product=newsroom.sgit.ai), site |
| **Where** | <https://newsroom.sgit.ai/persona/founder/> |
| **Problems** | [Hidden until script](/findings/?problem=hidden-until-script), [Dead end](/findings/?problem=dead-end) |
| **Visibility** | [Intermittent](/findings/?visibility=intermittent): some readers, some of the time: depends on a gesture, a device or a state, and is hard to reproduce on demand |
| **Recommendation** | [Render on the first load](/findings/?recommendation=render-on-first-load): show the content in the HTML, with no scripts and no prior visit needed |
| **Area** | [Personas](/findings/?area=personas) |
| **Breaks** | [Content is visible without waiting for scripts](/principles/index.md#content-is-visible) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, v0.7.1 |

# Persona pages are a list, with no story, opinion or next step

Open · medium severity · gap · newsroom.sgit.ai

## What we saw

Each persona page is seven starting articles plus an explanation of how the link works.

## Why it matters

A persona link is a promise that the site was made for this reader; a list does not keep it.

## The fix

One front-page template filled from a persona file: masthead, story, Dinis's note, start here, sections, board, "what is missing?", other readers.

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-046

# Setting location.hash inside a vault app re-navigates the frame: every link silently dead

Open · high severity · failure · dev.vault.sgraph.ai

## What we saw

In the host the app is an about:srcdoc frame, where assigning location.hash re-navigates instead of firing hashchange. The How Much Evidence vault shipped on 5 October 2026 with every view link dead.

## Why it matters

An app that works when opened as a file ships to readers with no working navigation, and nothing errors.

## The fix

Keep the route in a variable; catch a[href^="#"] in a capture click handler; mark links data-sg-native; use the hash only when running standalone. Documented in the sgit.ai guidance.

## The record

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Open. Open as a platform trap; every lab vault avoids it. |
| **Severity** | High |
| **Kind** | Failure: works against the reader |
| **Product** | [dev.vault.sgraph.ai](/findings/?product=dev.vault.sgraph.ai), platform |
| **Where** | any vault app that routes by hash |
| **Problems** | [Host trap](/findings/?problem=host-trap), [Dead end](/findings/?problem=dead-end) |
| **Visibility** | [Silent](/findings/?visibility=silent): no symptom on screen: found only by measuring, or by its consequences |
| **Recommendation** | [Design for the host](/findings/?recommendation=design-for-the-host): use the host's own mechanisms (route variable, sg.state, vault snapshot) instead of the browser's defaults |
| **Area** | [Platform](/findings/?area=platform) |
| **Breaks** | [A vault app works inside the host, not just on its own](/principles/index.md#host-safe-apps) |
| **Observed** | 2026-10-05, host |
| **Last checked** | 2026-10-11, host |
| **Source** | [Design lab: what building it measured](/lab/index.md#what-building-the-lab-measured) |

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-047

# localStorage throws inside the vault app frame, so reader data is lost on reload

Open · medium severity · failure · dev.vault.sgraph.ai

## What we saw

The app frame refuses localStorage with SecurityError. Lab kit v0.1.2 kept highlights, notes and ratings only until reload.

## Why it matters

A reader's notes disappear on reload, the worst failure a note-taking feature can have.

## The fix

Store through the host's async sg.state (survives reload). Kit v0.1.3 does; every lab vault was republished on it.

## The record

[Findings](/findings/index.md) / UX-048

# A vault app can load images and scripts from a site but cannot fetch its data

Open · low severity · gap · dev.vault.sgraph.ai

## What we saw

The host CSP is connect-src blob: data:. fetch() to newsroom.sgit.ai is refused although it sends access-control-allow-origin *, while <img> and classic <script src> from the same origin load.

## Why it matters

Builders reasonably expect CORS-open data to be readable and discover otherwise in production; apps must snapshot data instead.

## The fix

Snapshot the data into the vault (with SHA-256 in sources.json) and say in the UI which copy is shown. State the CSP where builders read about vault apps.

## The record

# Query strings break inside the vault host, so filters must live in the route path

Open · low severity · gap · dev.vault.sgraph.ai

## What we saw

Adding a query string to an app route breaks in the srcdoc frame.

## Why it matters

The usual way to make a filter linkable is not available; each app has to invent a path encoding.

## The fix

Encode filters in the path in a fixed order (desk, format, tag, series, month, q), as the findability vault does.

# File-path pills scrolled the whole page sideways at 390 px

Fixed · medium severity · failure · Newsroom Design Lab

## What we saw

Long, unbreakable file-path pills on the data pages pushed the page wider than a phone.

## Why it matters

Sideways scroll on a phone makes every line harder to read and hides the edge of the content.

Let pills wrap; the gate now fails on any sideways scroll at 390 px. Fixed in kit v0.1.2.

# Re-rendering the whole view on every save lost the reader's place

Fixed · medium severity · failure · Newsroom Design Lab

## What we saw

Every store write (a highlight, a note, a status) re-rendered the whole reading view and jumped the scroll position.

## Why it matters

A reader who highlights a sentence is thrown somewhere else in an 8,000-word article.

## The fix

Repaint only the parts that changed. Done in the article vault before publishing.

# Search results show no snippets

Snippets from the markdown twins, within a size budget, or computed on a site page rather than in the vault.

# "Ask the article" has never run against a real on-device model

Open · low severity · gap · Newsroom Design Lab

## What we saw

The ask view uses Chrome's built-in model when present and a labelled extractive fallback otherwise. Only the fallback and a stub were tested; the model is absent in headless Chrome and likely in the vault frame.

## Why it matters

The feature is shown to readers on a path nobody has seen work.

## The fix

Test in a real Chrome with the model, or use sg.llm with an llm.chat grant; until then say "fallback" in the UI, as it does.

## The record

| **Breaks** | [What a page says about the present is true now](/principles/index.md#state-is-current) |
